Hongbin Sun
Maoqing Yao
bullets: Addresses the limited settings and lack of independent validation in existing metric hand-labeling systems.
Uses calibrated stereo to establish metric scale at initialization instead of relying on monocular priors.
Assigns hand ownership during detection to exclude bystander hands from the wearer’s motion trajectory.
Evaluates hand and head outputs against independent Chingmu optical motion capture in a motion-capture volume.
Provides a pathway for collecting metric hand-motion supervision in more diverse, unprepared environments.
papers.selection_reason: Metric egocentric hand and head motion reconstruction aimed at learning manipulation from human video; directly fits embodied learning from human video.
papers.title: MEgoVista: Multi-view Ego-aware Motion Estimation for Metric 4D Hands and Head in the Wild
papers.tldr: MEgoVista is an offline pipeline that reconstructs metric, gravity-aligned two-hand and head motion from unconstrained stereo head-worn video.

papers.abstract: AI is beginning to make substantive contributions to LLM inference optimization. Existing AI optimizations are predominantly profiling-based. Profiling-bound feedback confines the search to the capabilities and performance of an existing software stack, preventing a fundamentally better architecture of LLM inference systems from being identified. To enable the AI-driven LLM inference system architecting loop, we argue that a general workload representation, a verifiable mutation space, and an implementation-independent evaluator are required. We present the RoofLang domain-specific language (DSL) that provides these features. In our evaluation, RoofLang reveals that DeepSeek V4-series models could achieve 3.5-39.5$\times$ higher peak decode throughput than other representative models. This gap is disproportionate to their total parameter counts and arises largely from compact KV-cache designs that support larger batches and reduce memory traffic. A persistent optimizer agent further discovered several new architectures that improved both throughput and interactivity of DeepSeek V4 Pro on NVIDIA B300 by 6.23-50.1%.
authors: Ziyue Yang
Yuting Jiang
Lei Qu
Peng Cheng
bullets: Addresses the limitation of profiling-based AI optimization, which cannot search beyond existing inference architectures.
Introduces a DSL with general workload representation, verifiable mutations, and an implementation-independent evaluator.
Finds that DeepSeek V4-series models could achieve 3.5–39.5× higher peak decode throughput than representative models, largely through compact KV-cache designs.
A persistent optimizer agent discovered architectures improving DeepSeek V4 Pro throughput and interactivity on NVIDIA B300 by 6.23–50.1%.
Scope: results are reported for the evaluated DeepSeek models and NVIDIA B300 platform.
papers.selection_reason: Domain-specific language and optimizer for LLM inference architecture, emphasizing KV-cache design and memory-traffic efficiency.
papers.title: RoofLang: Enabling AI-Driven Architecting of LLM Inference Systems
papers.tldr: RoofLang enables AI to explore and evaluate new LLM inference architectures beyond profiling existing software stacks, uncovering substantial throughput gains and novel optimizations.

papers.abstract: Recovering metric 3D geometry from monocular images is a fundamental computer vision task, yet current methods remain heavily fragmented by fixed camera model assumptions and inflexible input schemes. We present OmniPoint, a unified framework designed to generalize metric reconstruction across diverse imaging sensors, including pinhole, fisheye, and equirectangular projections, while accommodating varying geometric priors. To overcome projection rigidity, OmniPoint abandons conventional planar depth regression. It instead adopts a decoupled ray and distance representation alongside a decoupled training objective, explicitly separating the camera projection model from the scene structure. To address the severe scarcity of training data for alternative cameras, we introduce a bidirectional augmentation strategy that explicitly bridges labeled perspective data and unlabeled omnidirectional domains in 3D space. Furthermore, to seamlessly integrate optional inputs like camera intrinsics or sparse depth without destabilizing the network through feature distribution shifts, we propose a robust information injection mechanism. This mechanism utilizes learnable input state embeddings to resolve architectural ambiguity and applies vectorized Gaussian smoothing to densify irregular measurements. Extensive experiments demonstrate that OmniPoint achieves state-of-the-art zero-shot performance across multiple benchmarks, establishing a robust new standard for unified monocular 3D reconstruction.
authors: Botao Ye
Marc Pollefeys
Ming-Hsuan Yang
Abhijit Kundu
bullets: Targets fragmentation caused by fixed projection-model assumptions and rigid input schemes.
Uses decoupled ray-and-distance prediction and training to separate camera projection from scene structure.
Introduces bidirectional 3D augmentation to transfer supervision from labeled perspective data to unlabeled omnidirectional domains.
Handles optional intrinsics and sparse depth with learnable input-state embeddings and vectorized Gaussian smoothing.
Reports state-of-the-art zero-shot performance across multiple benchmarks, according to the abstract.
papers.selection_reason: Unified monocular metric 3D reconstruction framework generalizing across camera models; fits generalist 3D perception and foundation-model interests.
papers.title: OmniPoint: Universal Monocular Metric Pointcloud from Any Camera
papers.tldr: OmniPoint unifies monocular metric 3D point-cloud reconstruction across diverse camera types and optional geometric inputs.

papers.abstract: UAV video question answering requires separating camera motion from changes in the scene, but RGB-only multimodal models receive no explicit, stable reference for that separation. We present EgoSIS, a pose-free adapter that converts RGB-derived bidirectional flow into motion-canonical visual evidence in three stages. Factorized Visual Ego-Transitions (FVET) fits a robust image-plane transition and exposes motion, residual-support, and reliability factors. Reliability-Gated Ego-Transition Memory (ReTEM) uses reliability-weighted updates for a bounded history and re-anchors it at cuts or sustained uncertainty. Ego-Aligned Spatial Evidence (EASE) warps supported visual features into each segment's local anchor and injects four spatial evidence tokens per visual slice through zero-initialized residuals, without changing Qwen's visual-token count. On SIS-Bench, EgoSIS-8B obtains 89.9\% perception, 82.5\% perception-plus-memory, and 76.2\% overall accuracy, with the largest gains concentrated in self-awareness perception and memory. The adapter thus provides an interpretable interface between optical flow and spatial reasoning.
authors: Jingpu Yang
Fengxian Ji
Mingxuan Cui
Yilin Sun
Hang Zhang
Jianhua Zhu
Yufeng Wang
bullets: Addresses the lack of an explicit, stable motion reference in RGB-only UAV video QA.
Uses FVET to factorize optical flow into image-plane motion, residual support, and reliability.
Uses ReTEM to maintain reliability-weighted motion history and re-anchor after cuts or sustained uncertainty.
Uses EASE to warp supported features into local anchors and add four spatial evidence tokens without increasing Qwen’s visual-token count.
On SIS-Bench, EgoSIS-8B achieves 89.9% perception, 82.5% perception-plus-memory, and 76.2% overall accuracy, with largest gains in self-awareness perception and memory.
papers.selection_reason: Pose-free adapter for egocentric UAV video QA integrating spatial evidence tokens and reliability-gated memory into a multimodal LLM.
papers.title: EgoSIS: From Factorized Visual Ego-Transitions to Motion-Canonical Spatial Evidence for UAV Reasoning
papers.tldr: EgoSIS helps UAV video QA separate camera motion from scene changes by converting optical flow into stable, motion-aligned spatial evidence for an RGB-based multimodal model.

papers.abstract: This paper presents a general framework for simulating multi-body space robots with contact. We bring efficient, large-scale robot simulation to in-space servicing, assembly, and manufacturing applications. First, we perform an empirical trade study of methods for coupling orbit propagation with existing robotics simulation frameworks. Next, we present mjorbit, a general, flexible, and performant framework built on the MuJoCo engine widely used in robotics, to which we add key spacecraft dynamics, actuators, and sensors. We provide a low-latency C++ CPU backend and a high-throughput GPU backend behind a simple Python API. We demonstrate mjorbit by solving several realistic on-orbit case studies with both model-predictive control and reinforcement learning. Open-source code and examples are available at: https://johnzhang3.github.io/mjorbit/
authors: John Z. Zhang
Joris Verhagen
Fausto Vega
Patrick McKeen
Zachary Manchester
bullets: Targets in-space servicing, assembly, and manufacturing simulation.
Studies methods for coupling orbit propagation with robotics simulators.
Adds spacecraft dynamics, actuators, and sensors to the MuJoCo engine.
Provides low-latency C++ CPU and high-throughput GPU backends through a Python API.
Demonstrates model-predictive control and reinforcement learning on realistic on-orbit case studies; code and examples are open source.
papers.selection_reason: Simulation framework for space robotics with learned control and reinforcement learning; directly supports robot learning and manipulation research.
papers.title: mjorbit: A Simulation Framework for Space Robotics
papers.tldr: mjorbit is a flexible MuJoCo-based framework for simulating multi-body space robots with contact and supporting control and learning in on-orbit scenarios.

papers.abstract: Post-hoc sparse attention accelerates long-context prefill by routing each query to a small set of token-level interactions. Hard selection, however, assigns zero probability to every omitted chunk: a routing miss cannot be recovered, and a fixed expansion budget spends the same work on easy and ambiguous queries. We introduce Coarse-to-fine Error-aware Dynamic Attention Routing (CEDAR), a coarse-to-fine method that keeps the language model frozen while preserving global coverage. Each semantic chunk contributes a cheap key--value summary to a residual attention path; chunks with high estimated approximation error are then expanded to exact token attention. Exact and summarized contributions are combined in a single softmax normalization, so refinement replaces, rather than duplicates, coarse evidence. We derive an output-error bound governed by within-chunk key/value dispersion and use it to allocate a variable refinement budget. A controlled clustered-attention study shows that residual summaries reduce reconstruction error by more than 98% relative to hard dropping at equal exact-chunk budgets. Experiments on long-context benchmarks demonstrate that CEDAR recovers most of the quality lost by hard sparse routing while maintaining approximately $3\times$ kernel speedup at 128K context.
authors: Siyu Li
Dong Wang
Jie Zhou
Wei Li
Yang Xu
Sijie Song
bullets: Targets routing misses and wasteful fixed budgets in post-hoc sparse attention.
Keeps the language model frozen and summarizes every semantic chunk for global coverage.
Uses an error bound based on within-chunk key/value dispersion to dynamically refine ambiguous chunks.
Combines exact and summarized evidence under one softmax, so refinement replaces rather than duplicates coarse attention.
In controlled and benchmark studies, reduces reconstruction error by over 98% versus hard dropping and recovers most lost quality.
papers.selection_reason: Error-bounded sparse attention routing with residual summaries for efficient long-context prefill; fits efficient attention and long-context methods.
papers.title: CEDAR: Error-Bounded Residual Routing for Efficient Long-Context Attention
papers.tldr: CEDAR improves efficient long-context attention by replacing hard token dropping with error-aware coarse summaries and adaptive exact refinement, recovering most lost quality while retaining about 3× speedup at 128K context.

papers.abstract: Can exploratory UAV waypoint sequences be generated from multimodal onboard observations and a fixed-dimensional recurrent internal state without maintaining a persistent global map in the deployed policy? We investigate this question through CAVEAT, a diffusion policy conditioned on a recurrent internal state updated from fused LiDAR, visual, and pose features and trained from trajectories generated by the map-based FUELv2 expert. Rolling inference partially warm-starts consecutive predictions, while a temporary local signed distance field provides heuristic obstacle guidance. Simulation results evaluate both inference mechanisms and compare CAVEAT with its demonstration-generating expert. Proof-of-concept experiments on a Flyability Elios 3 demonstrate partial exploration of a previously unseen indoor environment and target-directed visual servoing using a separately trained policy.
authors: Steven Visch
Nicolò Botteghi
Antonio Franchi
Barbara Bazzana
bullets: Fuses LiDAR, visual, and pose features into a fixed-dimensional recurrent internal state.
Uses a diffusion policy trained on trajectories from the map-based FUELv2 expert.
Supports rolling inference with partial warm-starting and temporary local signed-distance-field obstacle guidance.
Simulation evaluates the inference mechanisms and compares CAVEAT with its demonstration-generating expert.
Proof-of-concept tests on a Flyability Elios 3 show partial indoor exploration and target-directed visual servoing with a separate policy.
papers.selection_reason: Learned diffusion policy for mapless UAV exploration with recurrent state and waypoint generation; fits robot navigation.
papers.title: CAVEAT: Recurrent Multimodal Diffusion Planning for Mapless Aerial Exploration
papers.tldr: CAVEAT generates exploratory UAV waypoint sequences from multimodal observations using recurrent state and diffusion planning, without requiring a persistent global map.
